summary:
On January 8, 2024, at 12:45, Liberty County EMS Rescue 14 was dispatched to the NSK plant for an industrial machinery entrapment involving Jonathan Davis, age 28, whose left arm was crushed by a metal stamping press. A tourniquet was applied by a factory responder and IV Fentanyl 100mcg was administered prior to transport to Midwest Regional Medical Center. At ED triage (13:28), the patient was classified ESI Level 1 (Emergent) with vital signs showing BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, and pain rated 10/10. He was admitted emergently to ICU-04 at 13:25 under attending Dr. Marcus Vance and admitting Dr. David Cho, with an admitting diagnosis of complete traumatic amputation between the shoulder and elbow, left arm (S48.112A).

Diagnostic workup included X-ray and CT angiography of the left upper extremity revealing extensive comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus, consistent with an unsalvageable limb. The emergency physician's impression was a mangled, unsalvageable left upper extremity with complete vascular and neurologic disruption and traumatic shock secondary to acute blood loss and pain. Two units of PRBC were transfused prior to transfer to the operating room.

Dr. Vance performed an emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; estimated blood loss was 650 mL, and a JP drain was placed (removed postoperative day 4, January 12). Postoperative labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2). Pain management included a Hydromorphone PCA, Gabapentin 300mg PO, Cefazolin 1g IV, and PRN Oxycodone. The patient was discharged January 15, 2024, after a seven-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg TID, Oxycodone 5mg q4-6h PRN, and a Cefdinir taper.

By February 12, 2024, the stump had healed but severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and hypersensitivity prompted a Gabapentin increase to 600mg TID and referrals for desensitization therapy and shrinker sock fitting. On June 18, 2024, a tender 1.5cm neuroma was identified, leading to a stump revision on November 12, 2024, excising a 1.8 x 1.4 cm median/ulnar neuroma with proximal nerve transposition into the triceps.

Prosthetic authorization was placed on hold in December 2024 pending insurer peer review, delaying therapy. Formal rehabilitation resumed January 2025, with a custom myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis fitted February 5, 2025. Therapy progressed over ten visits through June 2026, with two no-show/missed appointments (May and November 2025) attributed to workload and transportation issues. By discharge on June 22, 2026, pain had decreased to 1/10, with mastery of the prosthesis, independent ADLs, and clearance for modified light/medium duty work.
